column2: Precisely. Let us not give them my handwriting to transmit.
I'll process it, sir.
I assume you have not forgotten how to operate the Obscura.
No sir.
Good. Encode this.
At once, sir.
This is to leave the boat in cipher. See to it.
Yes sir. I'll check the request and prepare the encoded output.
I don't need a demonstration of the machinery. I need a usable message.
Understood, sir. I'll attend to the encoding.
How long do you require for this?
I'll need to examine the message first, sir.
A sensible answer. Better than a promise you cannot keep.
Thank you, sir.
I have rewritten this three times. You need only encode it once, correctly.
Yes sir. I'll take care with the message.
The contents are my concern. The cipher is yours.
Understood, sir. I'll process it under the current orders.
Can I trust this contraption to do its job today?
The Obscura is available, sir.
Then I will trust its operator to do the rest. Here is the message.
Yes sir.
Take this. It is for encoding, not for circulation around the compartment.
Of course, sir. I'll keep the contents secure.
I was told this desk is where plain language becomes a military secret.
I can encode the message for you, sir.
Then let us dispense with the description and proceed.
At once, sir.
Encode this carefully. Somebody on the other end will have to read it.
Yes sir. I'll prepare the output with care.
No need to spring to attention. Your hands are more useful at the machine.
Yes sir.
I have a message for encoding.
I'll get started, sir.
This request is for transmission. It has not yet been through the Obscura.
Understood, sir. I'll check it and process the message.
I need this encoded, and I would prefer not to return over an avoidable error.
Yes sir. I'll apply the required checks.
Your work is to make this unreadable to the wrong people.
Yes sir.
And readable to the right ones. Don't neglect that half.
Of course, sir. I'll encode it carefully.
I have a message to send. Keep the business of sending it properly in mind.
Yes sir. I'll attend to the encoding requirements.
Is your desk ready for a request from me?
Yes sir.
Good. This needs encoding before it goes anywhere near the transmitter.
I'll process it now, sir.
I would rather not explain to the radio watch why my message is still in plain text.
I'll examine it for encoding at once, sir.
Do you require anything before you start?
The message and its accompanying papers, sir.
You have what I was given. Tell me what the assessment is.
I will, sir.
This goes through the proper procedure. My name on it is not a substitute.
Understood, sir. I'll apply the standing requirements before encoding.
Be thorough with this one. Brevity on the page is no excuse for haste at the machine.
Yes sir. I'll give it the required attention.
I have an encoding task for you.
At your service, sir.
For the message, operator. Not for a ceremonial exchange.
Yes sir. May I have the paper?
Have this prepared for the radioman. He is to receive the cipher, not my draft.
Understood, sir. I'll process the encoding request.
Do you know what makes a good encoded message?
Accurate processing under the correct orders, sir.
A promising start. Apply it to this paper.
Yes sir.
I trust your concentration is better than the noise outside suggests.
You have my attention, sir.
Good. Encode this message.
At once, sir.
The transmission is my responsibility. Give me an encoded message I can account for.
Yes sir. I'll process it according to the regulations.
This is official traffic. Treat it with the care that deserves.
Of course, sir. I'll check the request and begin.
I will spare you a speech about accuracy. You know what is expected.
Yes sir.
Then take this message for encoding.
I'll attend to it immediately, sir.
The encoding is complete?
Yes sir. The encoded output is ready and cleared.
Good. I shall take this to the radio watch.
Yes sir. The message has been encoded successfully.
I can send this without returning here for a correction?
It has been processed and checked under the current orders, sir.
That is a better answer than promising miracles.
Thank you, sir.
All those keys, and the message emerges as it should.
Yes sir. The encoded copy is ready.
Let us hope the receiving operator is equally attentive.
Indeed, sir.
Is this the cipher I asked for?
Yes sir. Your message is encoded and accepted.
You have finished. And without needing my assistance.
Yes sir. The encoding is complete.
A fortunate arrangement. I would be very little help with those settings.
The output is ready for you, sir.
No irregularities that would hold up transmission?
The request is cleared and the message is encoded, sir.
Very well. I will see to its delivery.
Yes sir.
That looks properly incomprehensible.
The encoding is complete, sir.
I am relying on more than its appearance, naturally.
Of course, sir. It has been checked.
Prepared according to the standing orders?
Yes sir. The encoded message is ready.
I expect the recipient will appreciate a legible result after decoding.
The output has been processed correctly, sir.
Good. It would be unfortunate if my orders became suggestions through a typing error.
Understood, sir.
The message is fit for the transmitter?
Yes sir. It is encoded and cleared.
Then this part of the business is concluded.
Yes sir.
Excellent. One less plain text message waiting to cause trouble.
The encoded copy is ready, sir.
I take it you have not been offering opinions on the contents.
No sir. I have confined myself to processing the message.
A commendable division of labor.
Thank you, sir.
What shall I tell the radioman?
That the message is encoded and cleared for transmission, sir.
Good. He can direct his questions about the schedule to me.
Understood, sir.
Everything accounted for in the processing?
Yes sir. The encoding is complete and accepted.
You appear to have done that without breaking a sweat.
I followed the procedure, sir.
Continue to follow it. Looking busy is an inferior substitute.
Yes sir.
This is the finished output, not a practice sheet?
The finished encoded message, sir.
Very good. I have no use for a rehearsal today.
Of course, sir.
Ready for dispatch. That is what I wanted to hear.
Yes sir. The message is encoded and cleared.
Can I put this task out of my mind?
The encoding task is complete, sir.
The transmission is still mine, I know.
Yes sir. The output is ready for you.
I notice you have not tried to explain every lamp to me.
I thought the completed message would be more useful, sir.
You thought correctly.
Thank you, sir.
Good work. Give me the processed message.
Certainly, sir. The encoding is complete.
You are satisfied this meets the requirements?
Yes sir. It is accepted and encoded.
Then you needn't look as though I am about to inspect your bunk as well.
Understood, sir.
The operator at the other end had better be ready.
Our encoded output is ready, sir.
I can hardly ask more of this compartment.
Thank you, sir.
All clear for the next stage?
Yes sir. Encoding and the required checks are complete.
I shall take the papers with me. No outstanding issue?
None with the processing, sir. The message is encoded.
Good. I prefer to hear that before I reach the hatch.
Yes sir.
So this is what my carefully chosen words look like in cipher.
Yes sir. The output has been prepared correctly.
A humbling sight. I shall let the intended recipient recover the eloquence.
Of course, sir.
Accepted and encoded, then?
Yes sir. Ready for delivery to the radio watch.
You have earned the right to remain at your desk for the next task.
Thank you, sir. This message is complete.
That was an observation about naval service, not a reward.
Understood, sir.
I need the result, operator.
Encoding successful, sir. The output is cleared.
Excellent. Carry on with your duties.
Yes sir.
Accuracy before flourish. You seem to have remembered.
The message has been encoded according to the orders, sir.
Good. Keep that standard when nobody is standing over you.
I will, sir.
You are declining to encode it?
Yes sir. The request does not meet the current requirements.
My rank is on that paper, operator.
Yes sir. I still have to apply the standing requirements.
I know what you have to apply. I was hoping somebody else had applied them first.
Understood, sir.
So it is not cleared for transmission.
Correct, sir. The request is rejected as presented.
I was under the impression this was ready for your machine.
The request has not passed the required checks, sir.
Then my impression needs correcting.
I'm afraid so, sir.
This is an inconvenient time for a rejection.
I understand, sir. I cannot clear the request under the current orders.
There is probably never a convenient time.
No sir.
Do you mean the message cannot go out through your station?
Not on the request as submitted, sir. It is rejected.
I brought it personally to avoid delay.
Yes sir. It still has to satisfy the processing requirements.
Apparently I should have started at the other end of the paperwork.
I can return the rejected request to you, sir.
You are applying the same standard you would to anyone else?
Yes sir.
Very well. I won't ask for a worse standard merely because I outrank you.
Thank you, sir.
Not accepted. Right. I shall have to put it in order.
Yes sir. This request is not cleared for encoding.
I can assure you the message is necessary.
I do not question that, sir. The request has failed the required checks.
Necessity and clearance. Two separate headaches.
Yes sir.
The radio watch will be wondering where this is.
I cannot clear it for transmission as submitted, sir.
I will answer the radio watch. That is not your concern.
Understood, sir.
No encoded copy for dispatch, then?
No cleared copy, sir. The request has been rejected.
I don't want you to hide behind the regulations.
I am reporting the result of applying them, sir.
There is a difference. Keep it clear when you explain this.
Yes sir.
Would asking more loudly improve this result?
It would not alter the requirements, sir.
I rather suspected that. Give me the rejected request.
Certainly, sir.
This is going back for correction?
Yes sir. It has not met the requirements for encoding.
Somebody told me all the preliminaries were done.
I cannot confirm that from the request, sir.
Then somebody has confused optimism with administration.
The request remains rejected, sir.
You understand I am responsible for getting this sent?
Yes sir. I am responsible for the processing requirements at this station.
Neither of us has been given the pleasant half of this task.
I understand, sir.
I shall not send the radio watch an uncleared message.
Thank you, sir. The request has been rejected.
Is this your preference or a requirement?
A requirement under the current orders, sir.
Then say requirement. I have enough preferences to manage already.
Yes sir.
Perhaps I should operate the machine myself.
The request would still need clearance, sir.
Quite. A different pair of hands would not improve the paper.
No sir.
Rejected. I will deal with the request before arranging transmission.
Understood, sir. It is not cleared as submitted.
I expect you know how much work went into writing this.
I do not dispute the work, sir. It has not met the acceptance requirements.
Fine. I shall preserve the words and repair the request.
Yes sir.
If I send it back exactly as it is, I shall get the same answer?
Yes sir. The requirements would still not be satisfied.
A clear warning. I will bear it in mind.
Thank you, sir.
I have no use for a message that cannot properly be sent.
This request will need attention before clearance, sir.
You were not intimidated into passing it, at least.
I have followed the standing orders, sir.
Good. I would rather be annoyed here than exposed later.
Understood, sir.
This is not a question of whether you approve of the contents?
No sir. The rejection concerns the processing requirements.
Then I shall leave my speech about the contents for someone else.
Yes sir.
So the transmission must wait.
This request is not cleared for encoding, sir.
The officer who prepared this will be hearing from me.
I can confirm the request was rejected, sir.
I wasn't asking you to nominate a culprit.
Understood, sir.
I presume you are not suggesting I ignore the orders.
No sir. I am required to reject the request as presented.
Very well. We will have it corrected.
Yes sir.
Give me a short answer. Can this be sent as cleared traffic?
No sir. The encoding request has failed the required checks.
That will do. I shall attend to it.
Understood, sir.
At ease. I need this cipher made readable.
Yes sir. I'll examine the message and begin decoding.
You deal with the machinery. I will deal with what comes out of it.
Understood, sir. May I have the message?
I have a page full of letters and no useful way to read them.
A decoding task, sir?
